title: vLLM structured_outputs.regex -- T1499 uncompiled-timeout adversarial regex hangs an inference worker
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-55574 (GHSA-rwxx-mrjm-wc2m,
CVSS 8.7 HIGH), affecting vLLM prior to 0.24.0.

The `structured_outputs.regex` API parameter passes a user-supplied
regular expression string directly to the grammar-compiler backends
with NO COMPILATION TIMEOUT. In the `xgrammar` backend, the string
reaches the regex compiler with no guard at all. In the `outlines`
backend, the validation step blocks structurally-unsafe constructs
(lookarounds, backreferences) but performs NO COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS -- so
a pattern built from nested quantifiers (classic ReDoS shape) passes
every structural check while still causing exponential state-space
expansion during compilation. A single request carrying such an
adversarial regex hangs the inference worker that compiles it
INDEFINITELY, denying service to every other request queued behind it.

Detection logic flags a `structured_outputs.regex` request whose
pattern contains nested quantifiers -- e.g. `(a+)+`, `(a*)*`,
`(a+){2,}` shapes -- the specific construction that defeats the
`outlines` backend's structural-only check while still exploding
combinatorially.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (vllm-project,
via GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit and PR), fixed in 0.24.0
(adds a compilation timeout).
